options.text: Soorya walked to college every day.
Soorya have walked to college every day.
Soorya is walking to college every day.
Soorya walk to college every day.

questions.solution:

__

• To convey a habitual action, the correct verb form should be "**walked**".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Soorya** walked **to college every day."*

• **Option 4: "Soorya walk to college every day," **– This option is incorrect because "walk" should be in the past tense "walked" to indicate a habitual action in the past.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells goods at 40% loss on cost price but uses 25% less weight. What is his percentage profit or loss?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The shopkeeper sells goods at a 40% loss on cost price.

The shopkeeper uses 25% less weight.

Effective Profit or Loss Percentage = [(Loss% on Cost Price) / (1 - Fractional Reduction in Weight)]

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) at 40% loss = CP - 40% of CP

⇒ SP = 100 - 40

⇒ SP = 60 units

Actual weight used = 75% of the original weight

Fractional reduction in weight = 25% = 0.25

Effective Selling Price (considering 25% less weight) = SP / 0.75

⇒ Effective SP = 60 / 0.75

⇒ Effective SP = 80 units

Percentage Profit or Loss = [(Effective SP - CP) / CP] × 100

⇒ Percentage Profit or Loss = [(80 - 100) / 100] × 100

⇒ Percentage Profit or Loss = -20%

**The shopkeeper incurs a 20% loss.**

questions.question: Which of the following isotopes is used as a fuel in nuclear power plants for generating electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uranium - 235**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uranium-235 (U-235)** is a fissile isotope, meaning it can sustain a chain reaction of nuclear fission.
 
• U-235 is used as fuel in **nuclear power plants** to generate electricity.
 
• It is one of the few materials that can undergo nuclear fission, making it crucial for nuclear reactors and nuclear weapons.
 
• Uranium-235 is naturally occurring, but only about **0.7% of natural uranium** is U-235, the rest being Uranium-238.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear Fission**

 
 
• It is the process of splitting a heavy nucleus into two lighter nuclei, accompanied by the release of a large amount of energy.
 
• In a nuclear reactor, when a U-235 nucleus absorbs a neutron, it becomes unstable and splits, releasing energy, more neutrons, and fission products.
 
• The additional neutrons can further induce fission in other U-235 nuclei, creating a self-sustaining chain reaction.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Power Plants**
 
 
• These facilities use the heat generated from nuclear fission to produce steam, which drives turbines connected to generators, thus producing electricity.
 
• They are considered a low carbon energy source as they do not produce carbon dioxide during operation, unlike fossil fuel-based power plants.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.
 
• This results in different atomic masses for the isotopes of the same element.
 
 
 
• **Uranium Enrichment**
 
 
• The process of increasing the proportion of U-235 in natural uranium to make it suitable for use in nuclear reactors or weapons.
 
• Enrichment is typically required because natural uranium's U-235 content is too low for most nuclear reactors.
 
• Common methods of enrichment include gas centrifuge and gaseous diffusion.

questions.question: In which year did Swami Vivekananda give his speech at the Chicago Parliament of Religions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1893**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda delivered his famous speech at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago on **11th September 1893**.
 
• His speech began with the words "Sisters and Brothers of America," which received a standing ovation from the audience.
 
• The speech is considered a watershed moment in the history of India's religious and cultural influence on the West.
 
• Swami Vivekananda emphasized the importance of religious tolerance and universal acceptance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliament of Religions**

 
 
• The Parliament of Religions was an event held in 1893 as part of the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago.
 
• It aimed to create a global dialogue on religious matters and promote understanding between different faiths.
 
• It was the first formal gathering of representatives from Eastern and Western spiritual traditions.
 
 
 
• **Swami Vivekananda**
 
 
• Born as Narendranath Datta on 12th January 1863, Swami Vivekananda was a key figure in introducing Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world.
 
• He was a chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna.
 
• Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission and the Ramakrishna Math, which continue to promote his teachings and humanitarian activities.
 
• He played a significant role in the revival of Hinduism in India and contributed to the concept of nationalism in colonial India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Speech**
 
 
• The speech marked the beginning of global recognition for Indian spirituality and philosophy.
 
• It helped dispel many prejudices about Indian culture and religion in the West.
 
• Swami Vivekananda's address is often cited as a pivotal moment in the history of interfaith dialogue.

questions.question: Which Commission drew the boundary line between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radcliffe Boundary Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Radcliffe Boundary Commission was established in 1947 to demarcate the boundary between India and Pakistan.
 
• The commission was chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer.
 
• It was formed as part of the Indian Independence Act 1947, which led to the partition of British India.
 
• The boundary line drawn by the Radcliffe Commission is known as the Radcliffe Line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hilton Young Commission**

 
 
• Also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, it was established in 1926.
 
• It played a significant role in the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India in 1935.
 
 
 
• **Bretton Woods Commission**
 
 
• The Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 led to the establishment of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
 
• It played a crucial role in shaping the post-World War II global economic order.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Irwin Pact**
 
 
• Signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• The pact marked the end of the civil disobedience movement and led to the release of political prisoners.
 
 
 
• **Radcliffe Line**
 
 
• The Radcliffe Line is the boundary demarcation line between India and Pakistan, drawn in 1947 upon the Partition of India.
 
• The line divides the Indian subcontinent into two nations: India and Pakistan.
 
• The demarcation was based on religious majorities, with areas predominantly Muslim becoming part of Pakistan and areas predominantly Hindu remaining in India.
 
• It led to one of the largest mass migrations in human history and significant violence and turmoil.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties of Citizens were introduced by the 42nd Amendment in the year:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties of Citizens were introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act in the year **1976**.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the period of Emergency in India (1975-1977).
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, ten Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact on the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was passed during the period of Emergency under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.
 
• Besides introducing Fundamental Duties, it also made significant changes to the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and the structure of the Parliament and Judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• These duties are intended to remind citizens of their moral obligations towards the nation and fellow citizens.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• Initially, there were ten Fundamental Duties, but the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added one more duty, making the total count eleven.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• This committee was constituted in 1976 to make recommendations for the inclusion of Fundamental Duties and other constitutional changes.
 
• It was headed by Swaran Singh, a senior Congress leader and former Union Minister.
 
• The committee's recommendations led to the incorporation of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Emergency (1975-1977):**
 
 
• It was a 21-month period when President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, upon the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, declared a state of emergency across the country.
 
• During this period, civil liberties were suspended, and many political opponents were imprisoned.
 
• This period saw significant constitutional changes, including the 42nd Amendment Act.

questions.question: The Parliament of India has passed the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002, which establishes the basic rights of primary education for children between:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 - 14 Years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act was passed by the Parliament of India in December 2002, and it came into effect on July 1, 2003.
 
• This amendment inserted Article 21A in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It made it mandatory for the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children in this age group.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, was enacted to operationalize this constitutional mandate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendment:**

 
 
• A constitutional amendment is a change made to the Constitution of a country, which requires a specific procedure to be followed for its adoption.
 
• In India, a constitutional amendment requires a special majority in both houses of Parliament and, in certain cases, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A:**
 
 
• Article 21A was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
 
• It stipulates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years in a manner determined by law.
 
 
 
• **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009:**
 
 
• The RTE Act was enacted to give effect to Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It mandates that every child has a right to full-time elementary education of satisfactory and equitable quality in a formal school which satisfies certain essential norms and standards.
 
• It also lays down the responsibilities of the State, parents, schools, and teachers to ensure the implementation of this right.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Amendment:**
 
 
• This amendment has significantly increased the enrollment rates in primary schools across India.
 
• It has also brought attention to issues such as infrastructure, quality of education, and teacher training in the Indian educational system.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement/(s) is /are true with respect to Supreme Court Observation in A.G. Perarivalan vs The State Of Tamil Nadu State?

1. It highlighted that the Governor’s powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers

2. The bench headed by justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.

3. The bench was of the opinion that there are three sources of power-Governor, Council of Ministers and the Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Governor's Powers:** The Supreme Court highlighted that the Governor's powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers.
 
• **Convict's Release:** The bench headed by Justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.
 
• **Bench Composition:** The Supreme Court bench included Justice L Nageswara Rao and other justices who were instrumental in making the decision regarding the convict's release.
 
• **Constitutional Mandate:** The observations made by the Supreme Court emphasized the constitutional mandate that guides the Governor's actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role:**

 
 
• The Governor of a state in India acts as the nominal head, while the real powers of governance lie with the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The Governor's actions and decisions are generally based on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in certain exceptional situations where they may act at their discretion.
 
 
 
• **Rajiv Gandhi Assassination Case:**
 
 
• Rajiv Gandhi, the former Prime Minister of India, was assassinated on May 21, 1991, by a suicide bomber from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
 
• Several individuals were convicted in connection with the assassination, and the case has seen numerous legal proceedings over the years.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court's Observations:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court's observations in this case underscore the importance of constitutional principles in guiding the actions of state authorities, including the Governor.
 
• The case highlights the delicate balance of power between the different branches of government and the role of the judiciary in upholding constitutional mandates.
